rows.original_queue_goal: Ship the Relay 2.0 live React experience as the complete implementation lane for all discussed unowned release work: Today, Runner, night shift, shared card/signal-deck design, truthful telemetry/live progress, Inspector floating-QA polish, and the durable Inspector-to-worker feedback loop, while preserving the separate active ChatGPT inline-card clean-room lane.
rows.original_queue_acceptance: Relay 2.0 ships a Vite + React + TypeScript frontend boundary with ephemeral build output and the existing backend retained unless a bounded change is required. Momo Trust Display is the display/identity face for page titles, feature names and major card headings; Inter remains body/control/metadata type. Preserve lowercase feature identity, dark Terra Prime surfaces, chunky marks, rounded cards and no gradients. The corrected shared card family keeps a strong ~76px-scale mark, only modestly smaller feature name, tighter geometry, and no redundant small 'relay' eyebrow. Primary pages use a compact signal deck derived from that family: two cards side-by-side when space allows, horizontal pan/scroll-snap, restrained idle advance, pause on interaction, reduced-motion support, and no critical state hidden behind cycling. Today explains needs-you, moving, ready-to-review and freshness plus the most useful next action. Runner uses human-readable horizontal work cards with recognizable goals, plain-language state, responsible worker, next step, technical identity behind disclosure, and exact-work live progress views. Runner telemetry may include honest milestone-based percentage rings, bars, activity/milestone graphs, status/freshness lights and a latest-update ticker; numeric progress must expose its basis and never rise from elapsed time alone. Live progress shows meaningful timestamped updates, next milestone, blocker/request state, and explicit live/reconnecting/stale/offline semantics. Night shift immediately answers whether anything will happen tonight; before/during it shows schedule, next check, included projects and automation status; after a shift it becomes a while-you-were-away digest of results, changes, review needs and blockers, keeping project health, run history, monitoring state and model-credit availability distinct. Inspector remains the successful verification surface, but its floating QA instrument gains a visible autosave state icon, responsive/collapsible usable mode, smooth reliable edge docking/restore behavior, side-by-side binary response controls where space permits, reduced-motion behavior and viewport clamping. Inspector notes/answers/dispositions emit durable identity-bound feedback events with monotonic ordering; active and resuming workers fetch relevant unread feedback at normal synchronization points and acknowledge it so it is not repeatedly delivered; stale/mismatched assignment/branch/evidence identity must not be silently applied. Existing 1.9.9 production remains available until explicit cutover. Do not modify the active relay-inline-card-cleanroom-20261001 lane or its owned files.

rows.original_queue_goal: Fix Relay inline cards that mount as visible ChatGPT MCP App frames in the browser but remain blank on later/remounted renders in the same ordinary chat, despite earlier successful renders.
rows.original_queue_acceptance: Reproduce the exact observed browser failure: ordinary ChatGPT browser chat creates the Relay MCP App frame ('Opening Show Relay status card', CSP off) but the card body remains blank, including multiple renders in the same chat after earlier successful cards. Treat visible empty iframe as a lifecycle/runtime failure, not a mount failure. Identify whether the failure is resource fetch/cache identity, ui/initialize sequencing, tool-result delivery timing, host remount/replay behavior, or an unhandled widget JS exception. Add regression coverage for repeated/remounted cards in one conversation and reload/revisit behavior. Card must render approved UI from canonical result on first mount and after browser revisit/remount, without relying on a one-time host notification. Preserve approved design. Rotate resource identity if caching requires it. Ship exact-head tests, deploy, refresh tool metadata, and verify at least three direct ordinary-chat renders plus reopening the same chat still paint. Research findings to encode in the fix: OpenAI's current plugin UI docs require the MCP Apps bridge as primary but still document window.openai.toolOutput/toolInput as compatibility aliases; official issue #195 reproduces ChatGPT web remounting a historical MCP App without re-emitting ontoolresult, leaving it empty after revisit; the current Relay v7 renderer only paints from ui/notifications/tool-result and deliberately removed the compatibility fallback. Add a defensive hydration ladder: standard tool-result notification first, current window.openai.toolOutput if already populated, current window.openai.toolInput for arguments, optional openai:set_globals compatibility subscription, then a bounded read-only self-refresh via tools/call when canonical project/assignment arguments are available. Keep this additive, not host-name branching. Treat resource URI as a cache key and rotate on any HTML/JS/CSS change. Desktop is not categorically unsupported: current OpenAI plugin docs and official example issues demonstrate MCP UI in the native macOS desktop app, so desktop non-mount remains a separate host/client compatibility gate, not an accepted limitation.
